nodes.summary: Explains string equality failures, choosing between single-line and multiline diffs.

nodes.name: _diff_text
nodes.summary: Generates an ndiff-based explanation of two strings with highlighting and context.

nodes.name: _cap_ndiff_input
nodes.summary: Limits the lines fed to ndiff to avoid quadratic runtime on huge inputs.

nodes.name: _notin_text
nodes.summary: Explains a failing 'x not in y' text assertion by diffing the found substring context.

nodes.name: _write_pyc_fp
nodes.summary: Writes the pyc header and marshalled code object to an open file.

nodes.name: _write_pyc
nodes.summary: Writes a rewritten module's pyc file to the cache, returning success status.

nodes.name: _read_pyc
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a cached pyc against source mtime and size, returning the code object or None.

nodes.name: _replace_code_filenames
nodes.summary: Recursively rewrites co_filename in nested code objects.

nodes.name: _fix_code_filename
nodes.summary: Fixes co_filename of a cached code object to match the current source path.

nodes.name: rewrite_asserts
nodes.summary: Entry point that parses a module AST and runs AssertionRewriter on it.

nodes.name: _saferepr
nodes.summary: Size-limited repr for embedding in assertion messages, with newlines escaped.

nodes.name: _get_maxsize_for_saferepr
nodes.summary: Determines the repr size limit from verbosity configuration.

nodes.name: _format_assertmsg
nodes.summary: Formats a user-supplied assert message, escaping newlines and percent signs.

nodes.name: _call_reprcompare
nodes.summary: Runtime helper called by rewritten asserts to build comparison explanations via the reprcompare hook.

nodes.name: _get_assertion_exprs
nodes.summary: Maps source lines to the assertion expression text, used for pass-hook reporting.

nodes.name: try_makedirs
nodes.summary: Creates the __pycache__ directory, tolerating races and permission issues.

nodes.name: get_cache_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the cache directory for rewritten pyc files, honoring PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX.

nodes.name: AssertionRewritingHook
nodes.summary: Import hook (meta path finder and loader) that rewrites test modules, conftests and registered plugins on import and caches the result as pyc.

nodes.name: AssertionRewriter
nodes.summary: ast.NodeVisitor that rewrites assert statements into code that evaluates sub-expressions and builds detailed failure explanations.

nodes.name: materialize_with_truncation
nodes.summary: Collects explanation lines from an iterator up to a budget, truncating with a summary line when exceeded.

nodes.name: _get_truncation_parameters
nodes.summary: Computes truncation budget from verbosity and CI environment.

nodes.name: _budget_from_config
nodes.summary: Reads truncation line and character limits from ini options into a TruncationBudget.

nodes.name: _truncate_explanation
nodes.summary: Cuts explanation lines to the allowed count and appends a truncation notice.

nodes.name: _truncate_by_char_count
nodes.summary: Truncates the explanation by characters when the line budget is not enough.

nodes.name: format_explanation
nodes.summary: Turns the rewriter's mini-markup explanation into indented multi-line text.

nodes.name: _split_explanation
nodes.summary: Splits raw explanation text into lines, respecting embedded markers.

nodes.name: _format_lines
nodes.summary: Formats nested explanation lines with indentation and operator prefixes.

nodes.name: assertrepr_compare
nodes.summary: Main entry building the comparison explanation for a failed binary operator assert, with summary line and type-specific details.

nodes.name: error.py
nodes.summary: Vendored subset of pylib's py.error that lazily creates errno-specific Error subclasses and provides checked_call to translate OSError into them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) to forward attribute lookups to a shared ErrorMaker instance.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Base EnvironmentError subclass for errno-specific exceptions, with custom repr and str built from the class docstring and args.

nodes.name: ErrorMaker
nodes.summary: Factory that lazily builds and caches an Error subclass per errno, and wraps callables via checked_call to re-raise OSError as those classes (with Windows errno mapping).

nodes.name: __getattr__
nodes.summary: Module-level hook that resolves names like ENOENT to the corresponding errno-specific exception class via the shared ErrorMaker.

nodes.name: path.py
nodes.summary: Vendored local filesystem path implementation (LocalPath) from pylib, offering path manipulation, file IO, globbing, visiting, stat, and import helpers, used for legacy py.path.local compatibility.
nodes.languageNotes: Large class with operator overloading (__truediv__, __eq__, __fspath__) and heavy use of overloads and lazy imports of pwd/grp.

nodes.name: Checkers
nodes.summary: Implements the predicates behind LocalPath.check(), such as dir, file, exists, link, and fnmatch checks, with negation support.

nodes.name: NeverRaised
nodes.summary: Placeholder exception type used as a never-matching except target when no errors should be suppressed.

nodes.name: Visitor
nodes.summary: Recursive directory walker used by LocalPath.visit(), supporting filters, recursion predicates, sorting, and optional symlink handling.

nodes.name: FNMatcher
nodes.summary: Callable glob matcher that tests a path against an fnmatch pattern, anchoring relative patterns as needed.

nodes.name: map_as_list
nodes.summary: Small helper that applies a function over an iterable and returns the results as a list.

nodes.name: Stat
nodes.summary: Wrapper around os.stat results exposing attributes plus owner and group name lookup through pwd and grp.

nodes.name: getuserid
nodes.summary: Resolves a user name or numeric id into a uid via the pwd module.

nodes.name: getgroupid
nodes.summary: Resolves a group name or numeric id into a gid via the grp module.

nodes.name: LocalPath
nodes.summary: Core path object representing a local filesystem path, with join/dirpath/basename operations, read/write helpers, mkdir/remove/copy/move, visiting, globbing, stat, pyimport and temp directory creation. Backs the deprecated py.path.local API.

nodes.name: copymode
nodes.summary: Copies permission bits from one path to another, tolerating platforms where it is unsupported.

nodes.name: copystat
nodes.summary: Copies file metadata (mode and times) from source to destination.

nodes.name: copychunked
nodes.summary: Copies file contents from source to destination in fixed-size chunks.

nodes.name: isimportable
nodes.summary: Checks whether a name is a valid Python module identifier that could be imported.

nodes.name: py.py
nodes.summary: Compatibility shim that registers _pytest._py.error and _pytest._py.path as py.error and py.path in sys.modules so the legacy py namespace keeps working when pylib is absent.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutates sys.modules at import time to alias vendored modules under the old py package names.

nodes.name: _argcomplete.py
nodes.summary: Optional bash-completion support for pytest's argparse CLI via argcomplete. Defines a fast glob-based file completer and a try_argcomplete hook that is a no-op unless the _ARGCOMPLETE environment variable is set.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines try_argcomplete and filescompleter in conditional if/else branches at module level, depending on the _ARGCOMPLETE environment variable.

nodes.name: FastFilesCompleter
nodes.summary: Callable completer that globs the filesystem for a given prefix, appending a slash to directories and stripping the common directory prefix like bash does.

nodes.name: try_argcomplete
nodes.summary: Hook called just before parse_args() that invokes argcomplete.autocomplete on the parser when completion is active; a no-op stub otherwise.

nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the _pytest._py subpackage, which holds vendored py-library compatibility code.

tour.title: Project Overview and Entry Points
tour.description: The pytest package is the public face of the project: its __init__ re-exports fixtures, marks, raises, approx and hooks from the private _pytest implementation, and __main__ makes `python -m pytest` work. Start here to see the vocabulary users touch before diving into the engine behind it. The split between the public `pytest` namespace and the internal `_pytest` package is the organizing idea for the rest of the tour.
tour.languageLesson: A Python package's __init__.py can act as a facade: it imports names from submodules and lists them in __all__, so users get a stable import path while implementation files move freely. A __main__.py module runs when the package is executed with `python -m`.

tour.title: Startup and Configuration
tour.description: The _pytest.config package is the most depended-on part of the codebase. It parses the command line, locates ini files and rootdirs, builds the Config object and drives the plugin manager. Argument parsing (argparsing) and ini discovery (findpaths) feed into it, and exceptions define how usage errors surface. Everything later in the tour receives its settings through Config.

tour.title: Hooks and the Plugin System
tour.description: hookspec defines the hook contracts (pytest_configure, pytest_collection, pytest_runtest_protocol and so on) that plugins implement, and config registers built-in plugins alongside conftest and third-party ones. Almost every feature in pytest, from reporting to fixtures, is a plugin responding to these hooks, which is why this step precedes collection and running. helpconfig and _argcomplete are small plugins that hook into startup to provide --help output and shell completion.
tour.languageLesson: Plugin architectures like this rely on well-named functions discovered by convention: any function named pytest_* in a plugin module or conftest.py is matched against a hook specification and called by the plugin manager.

tour.title: Session and Collection Tree
tour.description: main.py implements the Session and the main loop that turns the command line into a tree of collectors. nodes.py supplies the Node, Collector and Item base classes that form that tree, and nodeid.py defines how node ids are built. Building on the config and hook machinery from the previous steps, collection calls hooks to discover files, which is the first place user tests enter the picture.

tour.title: Collecting Python Tests
tour.description: python.py turns modules, classes and functions into Module, Class and Function nodes and handles parametrization. It is the main bridge between user code and the generic node tree from the previous step. The mark package attaches metadata such as skip, xfail and parametrize to those nodes, and mark expressions power the -k and -m selection.
tour.languageLesson: Marks are applied as decorators: `@pytest.mark.slow` stores a MarkDecorator on the function, which collection later reads back from the node. This shows how Python decorators can attach metadata without altering behavior.

tour.title: Fixtures and Scopes
tour.description: fixtures.py implements dependency injection for tests: functions request fixtures by argument name, and a FixtureManager resolves them and caches values per scope. scope.py defines the scope levels (function, class, module, package, session). This builds directly on collection, since fixture definitions are discovered while Function items are created.
tour.languageLesson: The @pytest.fixture decorator and yield-based fixtures are context-manager-like generators: code before yield is setup and code after is teardown, run in reverse order of setup.

tour.title: Running Tests and Reports
tour.description: runner.py runs the setup, call and teardown phases of each item and captures the outcome into reports defined in reports.py. outcomes.py provides the skip, fail and exit exceptions that tests and plugins raise to control flow, and skipping.py applies skip and xfail marks during the run. Together they implement the pytest_runtest_protocol that the Session drives after collection.

tour.title: Terminal Output and Built-in Plugins
tour.description: terminal.py is the reporting plugin that listens to hooks and prints progress, summaries and failure details. Neighboring built-in plugins such as capture, logging, junitxml and cacheprovider follow the same pattern: each registers hooks to add one feature without touching the core. This shows the payoff of the plugin design from step 3.

tour.title: Assertion Rewriting
tour.description: The assertion package makes a plain `assert` statement produce rich failure messages. rewrite.py installs an import hook that rewrites test modules' AST at import time, while util.py and the _compare_* modules produce detailed diffs for sequences, mappings, sets and text. This is why users write bare asserts instead of assertEqual-style methods.
tour.languageLesson: Assertion rewriting uses the ast module: the import hook parses the source, walks the tree, replaces Assert nodes with code that records intermediate values, and compiles the result, a form of metaprogramming at import time.

tour.title: Test Authoring Helpers
tour.description: The helper modules are what users call inside their tests: approx for float comparison, raises for expected exceptions, monkeypatch and tmpdir for environment control, and recwarn for warnings. pytester is a fixture-based harness used to test pytest itself and plugins. They are exposed through the public API from step 1 and many register themselves as fixtures using the system from step 6.

tour.title: Foundation Utilities
tour.description: The lowest layer holds code shared by everything above: _code wraps tracebacks and source, _io handles terminal writing and safe repr, pathlib and compat smooth over platform differences, stash provides typed per-object storage, and deprecated and warning_types define how pytest warns about its own API changes. This is why these files have the highest fan-in in the graph, and why they are best read last once you know who uses them.
tour.languageLesson: Stash uses generic typed keys (StashKey[T]), so plugins can store values on a config or node with static type checking and without attribute name clashes.
